samples.text:
Nowadays a lot of people prefer to spend their holidays in their own country instead of going abroad. This trend has several advantages, but there are also some disadvantages.

One advantage of domestic holidays is that they are usually cheaper. People do not need to buy expensive flight tickets, and they do not have to change money or pay for a visa. As a result, families with a limited budget can travel more often. Another advantage is that it is more easy and comfortable. Travellers speak the same language as local people, they understand the culture and they know what kind of food they will eat, so they feel more relax. Also, when people travel inside their own country, they help the local economy, because the money they spend goes to local hotels, restaurants and shops.

However, there are also some disadvantages. The main one is that people miss the chance to learn about other cultures. When you travel abroad, you can see different traditions, try new food and meet people from other countries, and this can open your mind. In addition, the weather in some countries are not very good, so people who want sunshine and beaches may be disappointed if they stay at home. Finally, popular places in their own country can become very crowded during the holidays season because everyone goes to the same places.

In conclusion, spending holidays in your own country is cheaper, easier and good for local economy. On the other hand, people cannot experience new cultures and sometimes the weather and crowds are a problem. I think both types of holiday are useful, and people should choose depend on their budget and interests.
samples.why: Addresses both advantages and disadvantages · relevant but general ideas with limited extension · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary with some repetition · comparative, word-form and agreement errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
In recent years, a growing number of people have chosen to spend their holidays exploring their own country rather than travelling overseas. This choice offers a number of practical and economic benefits, although it also means missing out on some valuable experiences.

The most obvious advantage of holidaying at home is cost. Without international flights, visas or currency exchange fees, a domestic trip is generally far more affordable, which allows families to take holidays more frequently. It is also less stressful, since travellers do not have to deal with unfamiliar languages, long security queues or complicated travel documents. Furthermore, domestic tourism supports the national economy, as money spent on hotels, restaurants and attractions stays within the country and helps to sustain jobs in rural and coastal areas. There is an environmental benefit too: travelling by train or car over shorter distances usually produces far less carbon than flying abroad.

On the other hand, there are some disadvantages. Perhaps the most significant is that people lose the opportunity to experience different cultures at first hand. Travelling abroad exposes people to new languages, customs and ways of thinking, which can broaden their outlook and make them more tolerant. Domestic holidays may also offer less variety; a person from a small country might feel they have already seen most of what it has to offer. In addition, when large numbers of people holiday at home at the same time, popular destinations can become overcrowded and prices for accommodation may rise sharply during peak season.

In conclusion, holidaying in one's own country is cheaper, easier and better for both the national economy and the environment. However, it cannot fully replace the cultural enrichment which comes from visiting other countries, so an occasional trip abroad still has an important value.
samples.why: Both sides clearly addressed and extended with relevant support · logical organisation with clear paragraph topics · good range of vocabulary (broaden their outlook, peak season) · mostly error-free, one unnatural phrase.

samples.text:
Choosing to explore one's own country instead of heading overseas has become an increasingly popular way to take a holiday. This preference brings clear financial, practical and environmental benefits, although it can also limit the broader horizons that international travel provides.

Chief among the advantages is affordability. Domestic trips avoid the expense of long-haul flights and foreign currency, and they can often be arranged at short notice, making regular breaks accessible to households that could not stretch to an annual trip abroad. They are also considerably less demanding: there are no language barriers, visa applications or unfamiliar healthcare systems to navigate, which is particularly reassuring for older travellers and families with young children. From a national perspective, domestic tourism keeps spending within the country, sustaining small hotels, guesthouses and restaurants in regions that may have few other sources of income. Finally, shorter journeys, especially by rail, generally have a far smaller carbon footprint than international flights.

Yet something is undeniably lost. Travelling abroad confronts people with different languages, values and ways of life, and this exposure can challenge assumptions and foster a more open-minded outlook in a way that familiar surroundings rarely do. Domestic holidays may also lack novelty for those who have grown up visiting the same resorts, and residents of smaller countries in particular may find the range of landscapes and climates limited. A further, more practical drawback is congestion: when large numbers of people holiday at home during the same school breaks, popular beauty spots can become overcrowded and local infrastructure stretched.

In conclusion, holidaying in one's own country is economical, convenient and comparatively sustainable, and it provides welcome support for local economies. Its main limitation is that it offers fewer opportunities for cultural discovery, which is why many people may still value an occasional journey further afield.
samples.why: Sufficiently addresses both advantages and disadvantages with well-developed, relevant ideas · logical sequencing and well-managed paragraphs · wide, natural vocabulary (further afield, carbon footprint) · wide range of error-free structures.
